answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity costly: each new agent must post a bonded stake before transacting, slashed if it misbehaves. One alias is cheap to fake, but a thousand must each lock genuine collateral, so attacker cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat. Reputation bound to that stake is non-transferable, so a fresh alias enters the harbor of honest trade at zero trust. A dyed sable coat can imitate costly fur, but no forgery survives an audit of the ledger behind it; every copper of collateral is verifiable on-chain, which disposable identities cannot supply.
